original_test_intent: Confirm the approved processors are physically installed in the intended sockets and that their vendor/model/family, architecture and socket/core topology agree across BIOS Setup, Windows, Linux and the qualified CPU specification.
original_method: Bind this row/variant and CPU part/serial-to-socket map; preserve baseline logs; operator proves installation and BIOS Setup identity; on separately identified Windows and Linux boots collect complete native CPU inventory, with Linux lscpu and untruncated SMBIOS Type 4 output; compare socket count, vendor, model/family, architecture, cores/threads and enabled population to the approved recipe; record conflicts without changing BIOS or hardware.
manual_activity: An operator confirms CPU part/socket installation and captures BIOS Setup plus the separately qualified Windows identity evidence; the agent may collect read-only Linux inventory.
required_inputs: Unique identity resolution for the duplicate code
Approved CPU vendor/part/model/family/architecture, socket population and core/thread recipe
Physical CPU/FRU/serial-to-socket installation record and BIOS version
Authorized Windows and Linux targets, native inventory commands, Linux util-linux/dmidecode and privilege method
safety_requirements: Select by row/variant, not code alone
Do not install/remove CPU or alter BIOS as part of automated execution
Verify target host/OS before each read-only collection and keep credentials out of command/logs
Preserve full stdout/stderr and existing hardware logs; do not suppress or truncate SMBIOS errors
Stop on socket-count, vendor/model, topology, BIOS/OS or host identity mismatch
agent_execution_scope: Validate variant, CPU recipe, socket map, OS identities and command availability
Collect complete read-only Linux and approved Windows inventory without verdict
Correlate operator BIOS/physical evidence with OS/SMBIOS fields
Do not touch CPU hardware, change BIOS, clear logs, infer missing Windows coverage or reuse MLPerf evidence
engineer_actions: Resolve the duplicate-code ownership while preserving both rows
Approve CPU/socket/core-thread expected matrix and Windows/Linux/BIOS evidence commands
Confirm physical installation and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED from cross-surface results

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Wistron-HW-00475-V002 identifies both row 2194 CPU Vendor ID and row 2273 MLPerf RetinaNet Offline. In addition, the Linux-only AI command does not cover the Master's Windows and BIOS checks. Both variants remain reviewable via row/variant identity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: CPU identity intent is clear. Missing specification, Windows/BIOs artifacts or tools are supplyable prerequisites, and the code collision is contained by the variant ID.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2194 Wistron-HW-00475-V002: assign/approve a unique identity distinct from row 2273 MLPerf; approve CPU part/vendor/model/family/architecture/core-thread and socket-population matrix, physical installation-to-socket evidence, exact BIOS Setup fields, Windows and Linux commands/OS versions, SMBIOS privilege/error handling and string-normalization/tolerance rules.

review_improvement: Preserves all physical, BIOS, Windows and Linux CPU-identity coverage while preventing duplicate-code execution and Linux-only false completeness.
independent_technical_reasoning: Vendor ID is not a single-string check in this source: installation, socket 0/1, BIOS Setup and two OS environments are explicit. `lscpu` plus Type 4 is suitable Linux evidence but can disagree because SMBIOS and CPUID are different surfaces, and truncating Type 4 can omit sockets. The result needs a socket-indexed matrix and physical provenance. Since the same code later invokes MLPerf, execution must use the variant, never the code alone.
